_comment: Inline policy for the `edullm-final-dataset-build` Batch job role.
Structure copied from 08-reservoir-ingest-policy.json, with the prefix changed to
`_ingest/final-dataset/*`. Created because the reservoir role is hard-scoped to
`_ingest/reservoir-dolma2/*` and a reservoir-NAMED role must not silently become the
final-dataset role -- the failure mode that produced seven separate traps on 2026-08-08.
aws iam create-role --role-name edullm-final-dataset-build \
--assume-role-policy-document file://infra/11-final-dataset-build-trust-policy.json \
--permissions-boundary arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/InternSandboxBoundary
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name edullm-final-dataset-build \
--policy-name final-dataset-build \
--policy-document file://infra/11-final-dataset-build-policy.json
*** --permissions-boundary IS MANDATORY ***  InternSandboxBoundary's
`DenyUnboundedPrincipalCreation` denies iam:CreateRole with a StringNotEquals condition on
`iam:PermissionsBoundary`. The deny is CONDITIONAL, not absolute: omit the flag and CreateRole
fails with `explicit deny in a permissions boundary`, which reads exactly like a capability you
do not have. Two agents read it that way on 2026-08-08 before checking the boundary document.
Every pre-existing edullm role carries this boundary; verified on edullm-reservoir-ingest.
NeverWriteValidatorTriggeringOrTerminalNames is copied BYTE-FOR-BYTE from the reservoir
policy and must never be dropped. It is the third independent guard against an accidental
promotion, alongside the disabled `edullm-landing-manifest-created` rule and
`edullm-validator:16` no longer carrying --promote. A build child physically cannot write a
key that triggers Gate A.
`ReadTheBootstrapWheel` is deliberately ABSENT: edullm-reservoir-build:11 is digest-pinned and
bootstraps no wheel, and an unused Allow is a standing hole.
*** BUT _dist/ HOLDS MORE THAN THE WHEEL ***  Dropping `_dist/*` wholesale removed access to the
54 MB 13-gram decontamination index (`DECON_INDEX_KEY = _dist/eval-decontamination.bin`,
corpus_filter.py:93), which every build child MUST read. The first smoke test died on it:
`load_index` RAISES rather than returning an empty index, because -- its own docstring --
"a build that quietly skips decontamination produces a corpus indistinguishable from a
decontaminated one; you find out when a benchmark score looks too good, months later."
`ReadDecontaminationIndex` below therefore names that ONE OBJECT: narrower than the `_dist/*`
it replaces, and it cannot reach the wheel. The lesson: a prefix is not its best-known file.
*** put-role-policy REPLACES THE WHOLE DOCUMENT ***  Any edit must carry ALL statements. A
partial document silently deletes NeverWriteValidatorTriggeringOrTerminalNames -- the third
promotion guard -- and nothing would report it.
*** A FIX THAT RELOCATES A READ INTRODUCES EVERY PERMISSION THE NEW LOCATION NEEDS ***
`ListStagedSourcePrefix` was added 2026-08-10 after it cost the whole math pillar. The history:
Nemotron-CC-Math-v1 is a GATED HF repo, so the build got a 401 no credential of ours can clear.
The remedy was to stage the parquet to `s3://edullm-landing/_src/nemotron-cc-math-v1/` and teach
`repo` to accept an `s3://` URI (corpus_read.py:560-690). That remedy was reasoned about as a
TRANSPORT change -- same columns, same filters, same dedup -- and `ReadStagedSourceParquet` was
added for the GetObject it obviously needed. What nobody re-derived is that the new transport
ENUMERATES: `s3_files` opens with `s3.list(bucket, prefix + '/')` because a staged prefix has no
HF tree API to ask for a file list. `ListOnlyFinalDatasetIngestPrefix` is condition-scoped to
`s3:prefix = _ingest/final-dataset/*`, so the ListObjectsV2 on `_src/...` was denied -- and a
ListBucket denial is NOT a GetObject denial, so the Allow that was added did not cover it.
Cost: indices 152-161 (all 6 nemotron-cc-math-3 bundles + all 4 nemotron-cc-math-4plus bundles)
each died ~5 s in on `AccessDenied ... ListObjectsV2`, losing 2,438 planned shards / ~61 B tokens
-- 6.5% of the corpus and the ENTIRE math pillar -- on the 2026-08-09 build.
The generalisable lesson, which is NOT 'add ListBucket': when a fix MOVES a read to a new
location, enumerate the operations the new location requires and grant each one. GetObject and
ListBucket are different actions on different resources (object ARN vs BUCKET ARN), and S3 scopes
ListBucket by an `s3:prefix` CONDITION rather than by resource path -- so a prefix-scoped list
grant is invisible in the resource list and reads as though it covers the bucket.
Deliberately a SECOND, SEPARATE statement rather than a second value in the existing condition:
editing `ListOnlyFinalDatasetIngestPrefix` in place risks widening or narrowing the `_ingest/`
grant that 175 healthy bundles depend on, and the two prefixes have independent lifetimes (`_src/`
is staging for gated sources; `_ingest/` is this build's output). `_src/*` is also the narrowest
form that works: it matches `_src/nemotron-cc-math-v1/3/` and `.../4plus/` -- the only prefix
under `_src/` -- and cannot list `_ingest/`, `_dist/`, or the bucket root.
